resources.string: Lets Fox Launcher open notifications and quick settings, lock the screen, show recent apps, the power menu or take a screenshot when you make a home-screen gesture. If you turn on navigation gestures, it also places thin invisible strips along the screen edges in other apps, to go back, home or to recent apps when you swipe from them. It does not read what is on your screen.

Fox Launcher uses the accessibility service only to perform system actions, such as opening notifications when you gesture, and, if you turn on navigation gestures, to catch swipes from the screen edges in other apps. It does not read screen content. Turn on \"Fox gestures\" in the accessibility settings.
Android stopped the \"Fox gestures\" service, which happens when recent apps are cleared. In the accessibility settings, turn \"Fox gestures\" off and on again.

MIUI ignores an app\'s request to close other apps in the background, so Boost frees what Fox itself holds and shows how much memory that really freed: never an estimate. To close another app, open its app info and use Force stop. Deep boost, under Shizuku in Fox\'s settings, can close other apps through Shizuku.

Android 14 and later, and MIUI, do not let an app close other apps. With Deep boost on, Boost asks the shell to close the background processes of the apps it would close itself, never the app in front, the keyboard, the phone and SMS apps, accessibility services or the wallpaper. It does not force-stop anything, and the widget still shows only the memory it measured.
Until Shizuku is ready, Boost works as it does without it.

Hides Back, Home and Recents by switching the phone to full-screen gestures, as the system\'s own navigation setting does: swipe up from the bottom to go home, in from either side to go back. The phone keeps it after a restart, and the system\'s navigation setting turns the buttons back on too. Other apps that are open reload when it changes. On Xiaomi phones, Fox does it without Shizuku once you have granted it secure settings over adb (see the README).

resources.string: The buttons show everywhere now, so these apps change nothing

While the navigation buttons are hidden, these apps keep them. When you open one from Fox, from the home screen, a folder, the drawer or a gesture, Fox shows the buttons first and hides them again when you come back to Fox. Opened another way, from a notification, Recents or a link, an app gets the navigation as it is. An app still open from before reloads once as it opens. Needs what the switch needs: Shizuku, or on Xiaomi phones the adb grant.
